units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration specification for refreshing execution isolation after plan acceptance, realizing approved child workspaces from a current base reference, and preventing an accepted-plan continuation or session from crossing Issue ownership boundaries.
units.dependencyDirection: The suite drives heartbeatService and issueService through real Company, Project, Issue, interaction, plan-decomposition, task-session and execution-workspace tables; it invokes local Git/worktree side effects through the Heartbeat path while mocking only the execution adapter.
units.keyDataModels: Issue workMode and responsibleUserId, accepted issue-document revision and thread interaction, IssuePlanDecomposition claim/owner/status, ExecutionWorkspace strategy and sourceIssueId, AgentTaskSession taskKey/session parameters, wake payload/context routing flags, and adapter runtime/context.
units.lifecycle: An accepted confirmation wake can discard a shared planning workspace and stale task session, realize an isolated worktree, and execute in a fresh session; decomposed child Issues retain only workspace strategy until their first run so they resolve the then-current remote base; an in-flight decomposition claim owned by another Issue suppresses continuation and forces a fresh session, while the same Issue may resume its existing accepted-plan session.
units.testAssessment: Five substantial integration cases cover shared-to-isolated refresh, delayed child realization after base movement, cross-Issue claim suppression for planning and standard work, and same-Issue continuation. They exercise a real database and Git repositories, but do not prove transactional behavior across interaction, decomposition, workspace, session and run writes; approval authorization, expiry, revocation or exact action/digest binding; concurrent claim acquisition; crash recovery during worktree creation; remote-base trust and authorization; cleanup/compensation; or rejection/cancellation. Several wake cases use unpersisted interaction IDs or trusted accepted flags in payload/context, so the suite does not establish that execution derives from an authoritative approval record.
units.designRationale: Separate planning from implementation by refreshing execution isolation and session state at the acceptance boundary, delay child workspace realization to avoid freezing an obsolete base commit, and use Issue-scoped decomposition ownership to prevent stale approvals or sessions from contaminating unrelated work.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must turn a human-approved plan into bounded execution without carrying stale Agent memory, code/data workspace state or approval authority into another Work item, while preserving a precise responsibility chain and reproducible execution base.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the approval-boundary workspace refresh, lazy child realization, Work-scoped session identity and cross-Work continuation guard. Company OS should drive them from an immutable ApprovalDecision bound to action, plan revision/digest, Work, responsibility contract, accountable human, Agent, permissions/data contract and expiry; reserve the claim atomically, materialize through WorkspacePort, record a base/workspace attestation, and publish state changes through a transaction/outbox with compensating cleanup. Wake payload fields are hints, never authority.
units.responsibilityConflict: Paperclip stores a resolvedByUserId on a persisted acceptance fixture, but execution routing can be activated by caller-supplied interactionStatus/workspaceRefreshReason flags and some tests never persist the referenced interaction. The plan claim binds an owner Agent and revision but not the accountable human, exact approved action/digest, permission/data snapshot, runtime attestation or revocation state. Mutable multi-table state and local Git effects can therefore diverge from the approval and evidence chain.
